full_judgment: 6. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, learned Counsel, appearing for the respondent Nos. 1-3 submitted that on proper discussion of the evidence and materials on record the trial Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs finding that the deeds in question are false, but without reversing such finding the appellate Court set aside the decree passed by the trial Court, as such, the judgment of the appellate Court being not a proper judgment of reversal liable to be set aside, since it has occasioned failure of justice; that late Badruzzaman, the predecessor of the plaintiffs and contesting defendants was an inhabitant of Patiya but without registering the deeds in question in Patiya the registration was made in Boalkhali Sub-registrar Office and in Chittagong District Registrar Office respectively which created doubt about the genuineness of registration, as it appears from those deeds the attesting witnesses in the two deeds, are same persons who are the father-in-law of defendant No.5 and maternal grand father of defendant Nos.1-4 which also created doubt about the execution of the deeds to gift; that in such gift or Heber under Mohammadan Law 3(three) conditions are necessary, namely, the desire to the donor of gift the land, acceptance by the donee and delivery of , possession, but in the instant suit no where in the record the said 3(three) circumstances or occasions are available, and admittedly the defendant Nos.3-4 are minors; that admittedly the said Badruzzaman, has got two sons the defendant No.5 and plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 daughters the plaintiff Nos.3 and 4, and only wife their mother the plaintiff No.2 and it is also available in the record that Badruzzaman, had been leaving with his only wife and there is no reason to transfer the suit land in favour of his grand sons by way of gift in presence of his two sons and two daughters by depriving them and there is reason to conceal such execution of deeds of gift to his wife and it is natural that in any case of such sort of gift the other members of the family should be aware. Moreover, the suit land was admittedly mortgaged with the Bank on 01.04.1975 and that mortgage deed has been exhibited as exhibit ' 1 -Ga' without any objection and a part of the suit land was sold by him to his daughter on 13.12.1978 by executing a registered deed which has been exhibited as exhibit- 1 -Kha' without any objection which proved that those deeds are admittedly executed, and in presence of such admitted deeds the question of execution of deeds of gift is not reliable. Moreover, delivery of possession in favour of the donees has not at all proved rather it is evident from the evidences on record that both the parties jointly enjoying and possessing the suit land with the other property left by their predecessor, as such, the trial Court rightly and correctly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs, but without proper reversal of those findings the trial Court, the appellate Court most illegally allowed the appeal by setting aside the judgment of the trial Court.
